title: Google Business Profile Automation: Complete Guide for 2026

facts.fact: The guide states that a connected Google Business Profile gives five tabs: Performance, Reviews, Request reviews, Posts and Business info.
facts.quote: A connected Google Business Profile gives you five tabs and no more: Performance, Reviews, Request reviews, Posts and Business info.

facts.fact: According to the guide, every Reputation tab shows sample data (made-up reviews, names and numbers) until a Google Business Profile is connected.
facts.quote: Every Reputation tab works before a profile is attached, and what it shows is **sample data**: made-up reviews, made-up names, made-up numbers, with a badge and a prompt saying so.

facts.fact: The guide states that customers cannot reply to a business's reply to their Google review, so a review is the only conversation Google provides in this context.
facts.quote: A review is the only conversation Google gives you here, and the customer cannot reply to your reply.

facts.fact: The guide states that Google Business Profile questions and answers are not one of the five Reputation tabs and cannot be managed through the profile management tool.
facts.quote: The Q&A section that appears under a Google listing is not one of the five tabs, so answering a question a customer has posted is something you do on Google.

facts.fact: The guide was published on 13 August 2026.
Review gating, meaning privately asking customers whether they are happy and sending only happy customers to Google, goes against Google's policies.
facts.quote: Don’t create a system that asks customers privately if they’re happy and sends only the happy ones to Google. This practice is commonly called review gating, and it goes against Google’s policies.

facts.fact: Offering money, discounts, free services or other incentives in return for a Google review is advised against by the guide.
facts.quote: You also shouldn’t offer money, discounts, free services, or other incentives in return for a Google review.

facts.fact: In the guide's example workflow, a review request is sent 2 hours after an appointment is completed.
facts.quote: Appointment completed → wait 2 hours → send review request

facts.fact: In the guide's second example workflow, a review request is sent the following morning after a service is completed.
facts.quote: Service completed → wait until the following morning → send review request

facts.fact: Review requests can be sent by hand from the Request reviews tab or automatically from a flow after an appointment or payment, via WhatsApp, SMS or email as a tracked link.
facts.quote: Review requests go out as a tracked link on WhatsApp, SMS or email, by hand from the Request reviews tab or automatically from a flow after an appointment or a payment.

facts.fact: Four fields (phone, website, description and opening hours) can be edited outside Google and pushed to the Google Business Profile listing.
facts.quote: Four fields can be edited outside Google and pushed to your listing

facts.fact: Business name, category and address are read-only outside Google and must be changed on Google itself.
facts.quote: your business name, your category and your address are read-only

facts.fact: According to the vendor (DMly), special hours change eight or ten times a year, around bank holidays and similar events.
facts.quote: Special hours change eight or ten times, around bank holidays

facts.fact: According to the vendor, Google has no scheduled posting feature of its own, so scheduled posts are held outside Google until published.
facts.quote: Google has no scheduled posting of its own

facts.fact: Google Business Profile posts cannot be edited once published; changing a post requires deleting it and publishing again.
facts.quote: There is no edit.

facts.fact: Deleting a live Google Business Profile post removes it from the listing permanently.
facts.quote: takes it off your listing for good

facts.fact: An Offer post on Google Business Profile requires a title and a start and end date, and Google will not publish it without them.
facts.quote: an Offer and an Event both need a title and a start and end date, and Google will not take them without

facts.fact: A photo is recommended for both Offer and Event posts on Google Business Profile.
facts.quote: A photo is recommended for both.

facts.fact: An Update post on Google Business Profile needs only a message.
facts.quote: An Update needs a message and nothing else.

facts.fact: A Switch location control appears in Google Business Profile once more than one location is connected.
facts.quote: Each location connects as its own profile, and once more than one is connected

facts.fact: The location selected with the Switch location control lasts for the user's session and resets when they sign out.
facts.quote: That choice is yours alone and it lasts for your session.

facts.fact: Incentives such as discounts or freebies offered for reviews can breach Google's policies.
facts.quote: Discounts, freebies and other incentives for reviews can breach Google

facts.fact: Google allows businesses to ask customers for genuine reviews and provides a direct review link that businesses can share with customers.
facts.quote: Google allows businesses to ask customers for genuine reviews and provides a direct review link that you can share with them.

facts.fact: The page states that businesses should not offer discounts, free products, or other incentives in exchange for reviews.
facts.quote: businesses shouldn’t offer discounts, free products, or other incentives in exchange for reviews.

facts.fact: DMly can send a customer a Google review request through WhatsApp or SMS after their appointment, and a delay can be added so the message arrives at a more appropriate time.
facts.quote: DMly can send a customer a Google review request through WhatsApp or SMS after their appointment. You can also add a delay so the message arrives at a more appropriate time.

facts.fact: Google provides official APIs that approved platforms can use to manage supported Google Business Profile functions.
facts.quote: Google provides official APIs that approved platforms can use to manage supported Business Profile functions.

facts.fact: Google supports the management of multiple business locations, and third-party management platforms can provide a central place to oversee them.
facts.quote: Google supports the management of multiple business locations, and third-party management platforms can provide a central place to oversee them.

facts.fact: DMly does not draft Google review replies itself, and the page advises that a person should read every reply before it is sent, particularly for complaints and sensitive feedback.
facts.quote: DMly doesn’t draft review replies itself, and a person should read every reply before it goes out, particularly for complaints and sensitive feedback.

facts.fact: The page advises avoiding tools that promise questionable shortcuts, fake reviews, or ways to manipulate ratings.
facts.quote: Avoid tools that promise questionable shortcuts, fake reviews or ways to manipulate ratings.
